[[slide:greeting]]
Hi Casey. Here is a quick recap of your 2025 federal income tax return, filed as single. We will go through your income, your deductions, how the tax was figured, and how the balance due came about, so there are no surprises when we sit down together.
[[slide:income]]
Your total income was $107,310. Wages made up $98,000 of that, and you took $12,000 in taxable IRA distributions. Interest added $310, and a capital loss of $3,000 reduced the total.
[[slide:deductions]]
There were no adjustments this year, so your adjusted gross income was also $107,310. You itemized, with deductions totaling $21,400. A qualified business income deduction of $1,800 lowered the figure further, leaving taxable income of $84,110.
[[slide:tax]]
The income tax on your taxable income was $13,240, and additional tax from Schedule 2 of $1,100 brought your total federal tax to $14,340. That is an effective rate of 17.0% on your taxable income.
[[slide:result]]
Withholding from your wages was $11,200, and you made estimated payments of $1,500, for total payments of $12,700. Since that was less than your total tax, the return shows a balance due of $1,640. An estimated tax penalty of $42 is also shown on the return.
[[slide:observations]]
Withholding covered 78.1% of your total tax this year, which is why a balance remained at filing time. The return also includes an underpayment penalty because the payments made during the year did not keep pace with the tax as it accrued.
[[slide:next]]
At your review we can look at adjusting your withholding or your estimated payments so that next year's balance is smaller, and we can talk through the IRA distributions and what they mean going forward. We look forward to reviewing this with you.
